free_tier.stated: 100,000 reads per day; 1,000 writes per day; 1 GB per account; 1,000 namespaces

per_object_cap.stated: 25 MiB per value; 512 bytes per key
per_object_cap.notes: keys per namespace are unlimited, so the value size is the object cap

retention.stated: a stored value persists until it expires or is deleted; a write that sets no expiry leaves the value stored indefinitely
retention.notes: the null is indefinite: no free-tier deletion clock is published; the daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC, and an operation over a limit fails with an error

egress.terms: reads are counted, not metered by byte; no egress charge on any plan

interface_detail: a REST API and a Worker binding; access through wrangler
tooling: wrangler kv; the Cloudflare API; a Worker binding in code
chaining: a read cache in front of a free database: 100,000 reads a day is 100 times the write budget, which is the ratio that makes it a cache and not a store

limits.value: 1,000 writes per day to different keys
1 write per second to the same key
25 MiB per value; 1 GB per account

limits_note: 100,000 reads per day are unlimited on the paid plan; the minimum cacheTtl is 30 seconds
reliability_note: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
confidence_note: the limits page was read today; no namespace was created.

evidence.proved: Free column: 100,000 reads/day, 1,000 writes/day to different keys, 1 write/second to the same key, 1,000 namespaces, 1 GB/account, 1 GB/namespace, 512-byte keys, 25 MiB values, 30-second minimum cacheTtl
a stored value persists until expiry or deletion, and a write with no expiry is stored indefinitely
evidence.quote: Data cached in Workers KV is accessible from all other Cloudflare locations as well, and persists until expiry or deletion. ... the expirationTtl option is used to set the expiration time for the cache entry (in seconds), otherwise it will be stored indefinitely

evidence.proved: the daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC and an operation over a limit fails with an error
evidence.quote: Daily usage limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC. If you exceed any one of these limits, further operations of that type will fail with an error.

notes: The asymmetry is the finding: reads are plentiful and writes are not, by two orders of magnitude. Any design that treats KV as the store hits 1,000 writes a day and stops.
